issues.body: The command substitution redirects stderr and ignores the exit status: `open_heads="$(gh pr list ... 2>/dev/null)"`. If GitHub is unavailable, authentication expires, the query syntax fails, or `gh` returns any other non-zero status, `open_heads` is usually empty and execution continues to push a new branch and create a PR. This violates the claimed `ONE OPEN RESYNC PR AT A TIME` fail-safe and can produce PR-per-tick spam during an API failure while an earlier resync PR remains open. The existing harness has no failing-`gh pr list` case, so it passes vacuously for this failure mode.
issues.fix_hint: Capture and check the status of `gh pr list`; under `--apply`, abort before creating a commit/branch if the query fails. Extend `scripts/tests/test_beads_export_push.sh` so its `gh` stub can fail specifically for `pr list`, then assert exit non-zero, no remote resync branch, and no `pr create` call.
issues.title: Open-PR guard fails open when `gh pr list` errors

verdict.summary: The git-plumbing path and destructive-export guards are thoughtfully designed, but the apply path does not fail closed when the GitHub open-PR query fails. A transient authentication, API, or jq error is indistinguishable from an empty result, so the cron can create another resync branch/PR despite the documented one-open-PR invariant. The end-to-end test stubs only successful `gh pr list` responses and therefore does not exercise this load-bearing failure mode.
